# 🔎 SPN-149 independent review A

## Decision and source identity

**Score: 100/100. No actionable findings or unresolved blockers in the reviewed candidate.** This is an independent, nonimplementing review of the complete committed change, including landing bookkeeping. The grade does not certify hosted acceptance or authorize merge.

- Reviewed candidate: `8ee824a9787c630f7c9b02263461280611f68d59`.
- Reviewed tree: `fe2cc7200da2b0333374ad0bef89e88085ab6bda`.
- Base: `04baabd6a68abe7c0b225f8699681532e2205b60`.
- Review date: 2026-11-13 UTC.
- Reviewer: independent agent `/root/review_a`; did not implement this change, edit the repository, commit, push, run a browser, or trigger remote validation.
- Working tree was clean before and after review. This report and the reviewer’s control-run logs are outside the repository.

## Rubric

| Category | Score | Assessment |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Ticket scope and acceptance criteria | 35/35 | The original ticket’s conditional investigation, declared bounded sample, observation correction, denial/closure negative controls, existing two-login journey, and historical limitations are all retained. Native execution is explicitly pending, never asserted as passed. |
| Correctness, data integrity and access boundaries | 25/25 | Acceptance requires an actual successful handshake, closure of every frozen target, no later established matching connection, an intact observer, and independent HTTP 401 denial. The retained journey protects the other login’s queued write, saved value and reloaded native value. Product authority and transport code are unchanged. |
| Meaningful regression protection and local verification | 20/20 | I ran the 18 focused controls on the exact reviewed SHA; all passed. The suite exercises the actual browser helper and rejects false positives, observation loss, overflow and cleanup failures. Retained typecheck/lint/backlog evidence is traceable to unchanged executable bytes. |
| CI and operational design | 10/10 | Existing suite owners remain selected; the added controls are reached by the existing Node test glob. Required aggregates reject missing, skipped, failed and cancelled selected work. First-attempt JSON attachments are preserved by the existing reporter/upload path. No routing, matrix or required gate is weakened. |
| Maintainability, documentation, process and over-complexity | 10/10 | The helper stays specific to this Chromium journey, adds no dependency or product policy, and bounds private observation state. Decisions weigh all four personas. Maintained documentation, original evidence, ticket deletion, completion accounting, generated index and repaired links are consistent. The safeguards have concrete acceptance purposes rather than speculative abstraction. |
| **Total** | **100/100** | **No deductions.** |

CI result status contributes no deduction in any category, in accordance with `AGENTS.md` and `docs/run-backlog.md`.

## Evidence inspected

I read the current `AGENTS.md`, `docs/todo/process.md`, `docs/run-backlog.md`, `docs/testing.md`, `docs/product/personas.md`, the original `docs/todo/SPN-149.md` from the base, the complete base-to-candidate diff, the maintained implementation record and every new evidence file.

I also inspected the owning browser configuration and workflow, CI dependency classifier and aggregate contract, `e2e/sync-network.ts`, `e2e/native-sheet-value.ts`, the relevant session/identity/transport/navigation implementation, and the pinned Playwright implementation for CDP events and JSON attachment serialization.

### Reviewer-executed local controls

From `/workspace/scratch/13a7bba7afec/spinel`:

```sh
PATH=/workspace/scratch/cece61e42934/runtime/node-v26.13.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH node ../validation/watchdog.ts ../validation/review-a-controls-watchdog.json node scripts/serial.ts node --test scripts/ci/session-revocation.test.ts > ../validation/review-a-controls.log 2>&1
```

Result: **18 tests passed, zero failed/skipped/cancelled, exit 0**. Node was `v26.13.0`. Execution began `2026-11-13T04:04:11.048Z` and ended `2026-11-13T04:04:11.444Z`; total watchdog duration was 396 ms, peak process-tree RSS 215,664 KiB, minimum available memory 8,443,384 KiB, no resource abort. The run used the shared serial runner and watchdog. I notified the parent when it finished so reviewer B could run without overlap.

Evidence files:

- `/workspace/scratch/13a7bba7afec/validation/review-a-controls.log`
- `/workspace/scratch/13a7bba7afec/validation/review-a-controls-watchdog.json`

### Source and retained-evidence verification

- All 14 SHA-256 entries in `docs/implementation/evidence/SPN-149/local-validation.json` match the reviewed working tree, including the helper, browser case, focused suite, shared fixtures, authority dependencies, CI plan, browser config, lockfile and pinned Node declaration.
- The recorded committed verification source `8ea691b2286a48e6344d46bd6fba0fd64ad6698e` has the recorded tree `20557e405e1fa5642ccdbf14aaef99d5d873e90b`. Its difference from the reviewed candidate consists only of the implementation record, local-validation manifest and grooming link. The executable bytes are unchanged.
- I inspected the actual final typecheck/PR-check logs, repaired full lint/dependency/format log and backlog-check log. Their pass results and resource measurements agree with the maintained manifest. The earlier `no-unsafe-finally` failure is retained and its fix preserves the primary error.
- Declaration commit `d98f7d6b22459b4a9aa7306ab054c8e09e02e5d0` exists and contains the declared hypothesis, exact runtime, two controlled orderings, stop condition, resource bounds and pending native sample. Its commit time precedes the one retained dispatch probe.
- The retained probe source hash matches its result. The actual probe log contains the declared close-first result of one close and navigation-first result of zero closes; it did not launch a browser. I did not repeat the bounded experiment.
- I independently hashed the retained original ZIP and its relevant DOM, screenshot and retry-trace members; every hash matches the maintained original metadata. The original report member hash also matches. The retained record correctly separates retry 0’s failure/DOM from retry 1’s passing trace and states that the missing original ordering cannot be reconstructed.
- I inspected the pinned-browser installation log: all five built-in download attempts failed with invalid ZIP data, followed by exit 1. No local browser pass is claimed.

## Contract assessment

### Conditional observation correction

`e2e/session-revocation.ts:26–101` attaches a separate Chromium Network observer before navigation. URL matching uses origin and path while dropping query credentials from retained diagnostics. Successful establishment requires HTTP 101. `beforeRevoke()` at lines 133–142 freezes every then-open matching socket immediately before the synchronous database revocation (`e2e/collaboration.spec.ts:457–459`). `isClosed()` and `assertRevoked()` at helper lines 124–147 reject absent targets, still-open sockets, reopening, observer loss, overflow and non-401 authorization.

Navigation and Playwright’s page-level close notification are diagnostic only. The two ordering controls and the live-socket/active-authorization controls (`scripts/ci/session-revocation.test.ts:65–178`) exercise this actual helper. This is an adequately demonstrated conditional observer correction; it does not establish the original incident’s ordering or a product security defect.

### Complete two-login contract

The browser journey keeps its 60-second deadline and five-second closure poll (`e2e/collaboration.spec.ts:371`, `:460–462`). It waits for both editors’ saved/online state and an established revoked socket before holding the surviving login’s write. The same journey independently checks protocol closure, sign-in and editor removal, 401 denial, successful forwarding of the held write, surviving socket continuity, a 200 saved-sheet response, exact stored cell content, absence of later matching frames during the queued-write/reload window, native cell content after reload, and a final 401 (`:430–508`). The existing development and production Chromium owners remain in place; no duplicate journey or browser project is added.

### Privacy, first-attempt diagnostics and cleanup

The new snapshot contains finite event kinds, relative timestamps, socket ordinals, counts and booleans. It does not expose socket URLs, request IDs, tokens or frame payloads. The 64-event and 16-socket bounds fail closed, and the focused privacy test injects secrets and verifies that neither content nor URL survives serialization (`scripts/ci/session-revocation.test.ts:181–211`).

The browser `finally` path releases held writes, drains interception, detaches the observer, closes its extra context, deletes disposable data and attaches its content-free record (`e2e/collaboration.spec.ts:513–561`). Each asynchronous cleanup phase has a five-second wait bound; failures do not prevent later phases, and the main test error is preserved. On an otherwise successful body, cleanup/attachment failures still fail the case. Listener teardown removes only owned listeners. The cleanup controls cover synchronous rejection, asynchronous rejection and a stalled phase.

I checked that the pinned Playwright worker keeps a body attachment in the test result and its JSON reporter serializes the body as base64. The workflow already uploads `playwright-report/*.json` on every attempt, so the unchanged artifact patterns preserve this new first-attempt record; an extra attachment-file glob is not required.

### Sustainable routing and bookkeeping

The new `scripts/ci/session-revocation.test.ts` is included by `package.json`’s `scripts/ci/*.test.ts` glob and the existing remaining unit partition. Its routing control verifies auth/session, transport, identity, navigation, shared fixture and helper inputs and rejection of incomplete selected work (`:305–345`). Existing broad routing selects all applicable owners, and no workflow or gate definition changes.

The completion list adds only SPN-149; the allocation counter and grooming date are preserved. The ticket is deleted, there are no dependent tickets left naming it, the generated index records 22 open tickets, its rules survive in maintained documentation, and the grooming link now targets the maintained implementation record. There are no product UI changes requiring a separate visual review.

## Every actionable step to 100

**None.** The candidate earns 100/100 on this review. There are no withheld points, local repair steps, hosted-only deductions or owner-decision deductions.

## Hosted acceptance and completion still pending — zero score deduction

The grade is a pre-publication review. The existing development and production Chromium two-login cases still need their declared retry-zero execution on the published candidate/tested merge, with every configured retry retained separately and natural recurrence reported accurately. All seven current-head gates and every selected worker remain merge prerequisites. The original failure stays failed; a new passing sample cannot establish its missing ordering.

The final PR or immutable receipt must retain both independent reviews, the exact candidate/tested identities, actual first-attempt diagnostics and cleanup outcomes, all run attempts and their dispositions. After any subsequent source, bookkeeping or base edit, both reviewers must revalidate the new committed SHA. No remote publication, gate pass, native acceptance or merge is asserted by this report.

# Independent review B — SPN-149

## Verdict and identity

**Score: 97/100. Two local repairs remain; no points were deducted for hosted CI status.** I did not implement this change. This review is read-only apart from evidence/report files outside the repository. It covers the complete committed candidate, original ticket, maintained implementation record, relevant ownership/routing code and retained evidence.

- Candidate: `8ee824a9787c630f7c9b02263461280611f68d59`
- Candidate tree: `fe2cc7200da2b0333374ad0bef89e88085ab6bda`
- Base: `04baabd6a68abe7c0b225f8699681532e2205b60`
- Working copy: `/workspace/scratch/13a7bba7afec/spinel`; clean at inspection.
- No remote branch, PR, browser test or full test suite was run by this reviewer.

| Rubric | Awarded | Assessment |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Ticket scope and acceptance | 34/35 | Conditional observer correction, bounded investigation, real closure/denial and downstream content contract are preserved. One setup-failure cleanup path misses the stated bound (B2). |
| Correctness, data integrity and access boundaries | 25/25 | No application authority code changes. Closure requires established matching protocol sockets and independent 401 denial; false positives are rejected. |
| Meaningful regression protection and local verification | 19/20 | All 18 focused tests passed locally. The existing controls omit a stalled detach during failed observer setup (B2), which the additional probe reproduced. |
| CI and operational design | 10/10 | Existing owners and fail-closed aggregates remain selected; bounded content-free attachments reach the retained JSON report. No duplicated browser matrix or weakened gate. |
| Maintainability, documentation, process and over-complexity | 9/10 | Small ticket-specific helper, no new dependency or speculative framework. Copied Playwright diagnostic source lacks the mandated full attribution record (B1). |
| **Total** | **97/100** | Hosted results are a separate gate and cost no points. |

The score exceeds the numerical threshold, but the repository's review/repair process requires both local findings to be repaired and the new complete commit to be revalidated before a validation push. Neither finding establishes an application security defect.

## Every actionable step to 100

### B1 — Retain the required notice for copied Playwright source

**Severity:** low. **Points:** 1, maintainability/process. **Classification:** local.

**Location:** `docs/implementation/evidence/SPN-149/original-13557930894-playwright-source.json:7–44`; missing corresponding entry in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`.

The JSON packages verbatim Apache-2.0 source excerpts from the pinned Playwright `frames.ts`. It records the source URL, commit and a short license label, but does not retain the original copyright/license header or describe the extraction/modification in the copied material, and the third-party notice inventory has no Playwright evidence entry. `AGENTS.md` explicitly requires the original notice, a change note and registration for code copied from any Apache-2.0 project; it does not exempt diagnostic excerpts.

**Fix:** preserve the actual header/notice from the exact pinned source in the evidence metadata, identify the modification accurately as selecting/packaging diagnostic excerpts with their code unchanged, and add the exact evidence path, upstream commit, license and extraction description to `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`. This does not require changing the experiment or executing it again.

### B2 — Bound failed observer setup cleanup and preserve its original error

**Severity:** medium; in-scope cleanup/first-failure evidence repair. **Points:** 2 total: 1 scope/acceptance and 1 regression verification. **Classification:** local.

**Location:** `e2e/session-revocation.ts:117–122`; awaiting caller at `e2e/collaboration.spec.ts:409`; related coverage at `scripts/ci/session-revocation.test.ts:214–235` and `283–310`.

If `Network.enable` rejects and `session.detach()` never settles, the setup catch awaits `stop().catch(...)` indefinitely. The caller has not yet received or assigned `observation`, so it cannot enter its normal bounded cleanup and attach the failure evidence while that await remains pending. Listener removal happens before the stall, which is good, but the failed setup still violates the stated five-second cleanup bound. The existing setup test covers a rejecting detach and the general cleanup test covers a stalled phase; neither covers the actual setup catch's unbounded await.

**Reproduction on the reviewed commit:** a browser-free EventEmitter fixture rejects `Network.enable` with an identifiable primary error and returns a never-settling promise from `detach`. At 5,106 ms the observation promise was still pending rather than rejecting with the original error. Detach had started and both owned listener collections were empty. This used the real imported helper, not a copy of its implementation. See `/workspace/scratch/13a7bba7afec/validation/review-b-setup-cleanup.log` and `review-b-setup-cleanup-watchdog.json`.

**Fix:** put setup-error `stop()` through the same finite cleanup mechanism (or an equally small five-second bound), then rethrow the original `Network.enable` error regardless of detach rejection or timeout. Add a focused mocked-timer test that makes enable reject and detach remain pending, advances the five-second deadline, asserts rejection with the identical primary error, and verifies all owned listeners were removed. Keep the current journey and assertion deadlines.

There are no other withheld points, hosted-only deductions, owner-decision deductions or impossible steps to 100 in this review.

## Evidence checked

### Independent local execution

After reviewer A released the shared test turn, I ran:

```sh
PATH=/workspace/scratch/cece61e42934/runtime/node-v26.13.0-linux-x64/bin:$PATH node ../validation/watchdog.ts ../validation/review-b-controls-watchdog.json node scripts/serial.ts node --test scripts/ci/session-revocation.test.ts > ../validation/review-b-controls.log 2>&1
```

Result: **18 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, 0 cancelled** on Node `v26.13.0`. The watchdog recorded 467 ms elapsed, peak process-tree RSS 231,136 KiB, exit 0 and no abort. Minimum system available memory was 8,464,052 KiB. This run used the exact candidate bytes.

The additional focused setup-cleanup probe used the same pinned Node, shared serial runner and watchdog. It completed in 5,388 ms, peak 154,804 KiB, exit 0 with no watchdog abort; its deliberate result was the pending cleanup condition described in B2. This is diagnostic evidence of the gap, not a passing cleanup regression.

### Source, contract and privacy review

I read `AGENTS.md`, all of `docs/todo/process.md`, `docs/run-backlog.md`, `docs/testing.md`, `docs/product/personas.md`, the original ticket via `git show <base>:docs/todo/SPN-149.md`, maintained `docs/implementation/SPN-149.md`, and the entire base-to-candidate change.

I followed current ownership through `AuthStore.revokeSession`, document credential validation, collaboration identity, sync transport revalidation/send and broadcast guards, and the native client authentication handoff. These application files are unchanged by the candidate. The helper is installed before navigation and leaves the revoked socket unintercepted. It requires HTTP 101 before targeting, freezes every open matching request before the synchronous revocation, and accepts only matching protocol close events. Sign-in/navigation and Playwright page close remain diagnostic only. A later successful handshake, a live target, observer loss or bounded-buffer overflow invalidates acceptance.

The browser case retains sign-in plus editor removal, two independent denied requests, surviving-login HTTP 200, the original queued write being successfully forwarded, no surviving close before its explicit reload, exact saved cell content, native reloaded value, and unchanged post-boundary frame counts. It strengthens the previous fixture-string check into absence of every matching later received frame without collecting payloads. The existing 60-second test and five-second closure budgets remain unchanged.

Diagnostic snapshots contain finite event names, relative times, ordinal socket numbers, counts and flags; no URLs, request IDs, cookies, tickets, payloads or document content are emitted. The 64-event and 16-socket limits fail closed. Cleanup continues through writes, observer, context and database phase failures, and primary test errors survive later cleanup/attachment failures. B2 is the one uncovered exception before setup returns.

I checked the pinned installed Playwright JSON reporter: Buffer attachments are serialized into each attempt's result as base64 bodies. The unchanged CI upload includes `playwright-report/*.json`, so this attachment is preserved despite the absence of a new standalone attachment-path glob. The artifact remains temporary (seven days); the implementation correctly requires the final immutable acceptance receipt to retain necessary evidence.

### Provenance, routing and bookkeeping

I read every retained SPN-149 evidence file. The two-ordering probe uses the actual installed Playwright FrameManager and demonstrates conditional map-clearing loss; it neither launches a browser nor proves the historical failed attempt's ordering. The records preserve that limitation and the missing first-attempt timeline. The retry-1 trace is not represented as retry-0 evidence, and the previously incorrect 30-day artifact claim is corrected to seven days.

I independently verified the original archive byte count, SHA-256, member count and the four listed revocation-member hashes against the locally retained archive. I also verified every source hash in `local-validation.json`, the retained probe hash, installed Playwright bundle hash and pinned Node executable hash. The declaration and executable-source commits exist with the recorded trees. The difference from executable-source commit `8ea691b2286a48e6344d46bd6fba0fd64ad6698e` to the candidate is confined to the documented evidence/doc-link changes.

The focused routing control covers the observer, journey, native-cell and sync-network helpers, auth/session, collaboration identity, sync transport, native client, application navigation and harness path. It confirms unit/browser selection and rejects missing, failed, skipped and cancelled selected evidence. I inspected the plan, workflow, package test inclusion and aggregate wiring: no routing or gate was weakened.

Only SPN-149 is removed from the backlog. The completed ID is appended while the allocation counter and grooming date remain unchanged; the generated index reports 22 open tickets, and the old grooming link points to the maintained record. The record weighs all four personas: Operator observability, Owner/Collaborator access and preserved work, and unchanged Link guest boundaries. There is no UI change requiring independent visual review. The helper and finite cleanup seam are proportionate to the accepted outcome; no over-complexity deduction is warranted.

## Separate remaining gates and limits

Pinned local Chromium installation is documented as failed because the official installer downloaded invalid/empty archives; no browser acceptance was run locally or claimed by this review. The existing development and production Chromium first attempts, their separately retained retries if any, and all selected current-head CI gates remain pending. Their status is not part of this score.

The native sample must keep the declared finite bounds and explicitly state whether natural recurrence was observed or not reproduced. Historical causality remains unavailable regardless of a later pass. After repairs, both reviewers must revalidate the same complete committed source before validation publication. Actual hosted acceptance, current base readiness and post-merge branch cleanup remain later gates, not accomplishments of this local review.

disposition: Both local findings repaired before any validation ref/PR publication; the changed complete candidate requires both reviewers again.
